questions.prompt: The quote is best bid 20.00 and best ask 20.10. You buy 200 shares at once and sell them at once a second later. The quote has not changed. What is your result?
options: No gain and no loss, because the price did not move
questions.explanation: You buy at the ask and sell at the bid, so you lose 20.10 − 20.00 = 0.10 per share. On 200 shares that is 0.10 × 200 = 20 pounds.

questions.prompt: The quote is best bid 49.95 and best ask 50.05. What is the mid price, and what does one immediate purchase cost compared with it?
options: Mid price 50.00; a purchase pays 0.10 above it
Mid price 50.05; a purchase pays nothing extra
Mid price 50.00; a purchase pays 0.05 above it
Mid price 49.95; a purchase pays 0.10 above it
questions.explanation: The mid price is (49.95 + 50.05) / 2 = 50.00. A purchase at once pays the ask, 0.05 above the mid price, which is half the spread of 0.10.

questions.prompt: Share A has a spread of 0.04 at a mid price of 100.00. Share B has a spread of 0.10 at a mid price of 5.00. Which is cheaper to trade, and why?
options: Share A, because its spread is 0.04% of its price and share B's is 2%
Share B, because its spread of 0.10 is a small number
They cost the same, because both spreads are below 1 pound
Share B, because its price is lower
questions.explanation: A spread matters relative to the price. 0.04 / 100.00 = 0.0004 and 0.10 / 5.00 = 0.02, so share B costs 50 times as much per trade, as a fraction of its price.
